correctness.rationale: The primary source independently establishes the two unique optimal densities with exponents 1/(d+1) and d/(d+1). Their exponents sum to one, so direct substitution in the standard squared-Hellinger formula gives the exact curvature-moment ratio. Cauchy--Schwarz gives the sharp upper bound on the affinity, with equality only for constant positive curvature. Differentiating log I_t gives the mean and variance of log curvature under the exponential-family measure mu_t, and a two-interval integration by parts proves the exact midpoint-kernel representation. Dilation exponents cancel exactly.

value.rationale: The primary theorem is driven by incompatibility of two canonical optimal vertex distributions, so measuring that incompatibility is directly motivated. Hellinger distance is a standard intrinsic metric on probability laws, and here it collapses to a closed, similarity-invariant curvature-moment formula for every C^2_+ body. The exact integrated variance representation additionally identifies what geometric inhomogeneity creates the mismatch. This strengthens a qualitative equality test without making an unsupported geometric-stability claim.
